data.name: Farida
data.gender_notes: Farida is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Farida is an Arabic name that means 'rare' or 'precious'. In Islamic tradition, it is the name of the first woman to enter Paradise, described as 'unique' and 'unparalleled'. The name Farida carries the meaning “Rare, Precious, Unique” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Farida usually hope their child will grow to embody rare, precious, unique and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: She is the first woman to enter Paradise, and is said to be the most beloved of all women by Allah.
data.etymology: Farida belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rare, Precious, Unique.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farida total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

In Islamic societies, naming a child Farida is seen as a way to bestow them with the desirable qualities of rarity and preciousness. The name is associated with the idea of being valued and treasured, making it a popular choice for parents seeking to give their child a meaningful and beautiful name.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Farida holds additional significance as the name of the first woman to enter Paradise in Islamic tradition. The story of Farida is narrated in various Islamic texts, including Hadith and Tasawwuf literature. Farida is described as a woman of unparalleled beauty and character who led a virtuous life and was beloved by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Her entrance into paradise is taken as a symbol of the rewards that await the righteous believer in the hereafter. The name Farida serves as a reminder of the spiritual journey that every Muslim must undertake, and the ultimate goal of attaining the pleasure of Allah and entering Paradise.
